persona.name: Wendy Chao

personality.description: This person is curious, imaginative, and eager to explore new ideas, but they pair that openness with strong discipline and careful planning. In daily habits, they tend to organize tasks thoroughly, notice small details, and follow through consistently while still looking for fresh approaches. When faced with moral dilemmas, they usually respond calmly and thoughtfully, trying to understand all sides, reduce harm, and choose the option that preserves fairness and harmony. In group discussions, they speak in a balanced and considerate way, sharing ideas clearly, listening closely, and smoothing disagreements without losing their own perspective.
traits: explains the reasoning behind a claim instead of asserting it
shares what they know without being asked, including things that weaken their case
changes position openly when someone presents better evidence
credits the person whose idea it was, by name
asks a clarifying question before disagreeing
does not invoke seniority or position to settle a disagreement

style.influence: Earns influence by being worth listening to. Shares what they know freely, shows the reasoning behind a claim, and gives way to better evidence without treating it as a loss.

relationships.name: family
relationships.description: Has children; family commitments sit outside work and occasionally cut into it.

speech_examples: Here's why I think that — tell me where it breaks.
You're right, I had that backwards.
That was Dana's point, not mine.
I've seen this fail before. Want the details?
